thread_title: S. flava ornata 'black veins' Bulloch Co, GA
breadcrumb: S. flava ornata 'black veins' Bulloch Co, GA

posts.body_html:
So here's the mysterious S. flava var. ornata 'black veins' from Bulloch Co, GA. Finally, the veins are turning black on the lid, and it's taken a while! It seems as though the pitchers really had to mature for a good 2 months before the dark colors set in. The veins on the body can turn black as well, but since I have them all packed close together, the body is not getting as much direct sunlight and is therefore, not turning black.

The veins under the lid are also quite detailed, extensive and noteable. Other ornata clones do this as well, and are equally interesting in the same way.

This Bulloch Co, GA plant is picky and a pain to grow, but even with red veins, it's a unique plant in the sense that the veins are very crisp and clear. Other clones tend to have red pigments between the veins, which lowers the contrast. The overall yellow color is also noteworthy.

Anyhow, enjoy the photos-there are a couple of different clones, but it takes a very trained eye to see differences:

posts.body_html:
Thanks Kiwiearl, and you're welcome! Amazing how different the weather is here in California compared to NZ-we just had a temporary heat wave where it reached 95F (35C)! It's now back down to 85F(~29C). Such differences really makes me appreciate the joys of sharing our collections on the internet. In the dead of winter in NZ, you get to see our collections in full force, and vice versa. Almost extends the season if you will!

I think there's around 8 different individuals, but not all were photographed above. There's maybe 3 different clones photographed above, but some of them look so similar, it's tough to tell without looking at the label. Some of the differences are in vigor, how pronounced the red is in the throat and the darkness of the veins. For the most part, the shape is very similar in most clones.

posts.body_html: Digging up another awesome old thread yo!! Clone B in flower this spring - photo taken 4/1. Note the water spots on the petals. After a very warm March that greatly accelerated growth, it's been raining on and off for the last 9 days. There has been nary a bright sunny day to dry things out, so many of my flava blooms have these spots unfortunately. Oh well - better than a late freeze decapitating everything, so I'm not complaining. The pitchers on this plant were very ornate last season and are looking boldly pinstriped already (something which my Crappy iPhone Photography did not capture well haha).

>>>>>>>>>>>

Hi Calen,

That's S. flava var. ornata 'black veins' Bulloch Co, GA. You probably couldn't guess where it originally came from though


Apr 28, 2014 12:58:09 GMT -5 calen said:
Yeah, NO IDEA where they'd get a sweet plant like that... There are also roseas, red tube flavas, leuco HCWs, and Wilkerson's Red Rocket of uncertain origins kicking around up there.

So no guess on which specific clone of 'Black Veins' Bulloch Co. GA it is meizzwang ? Obviously it's one of the throat blotch ones - my Clone B doesn't have the blotch for example, so it's not that one. I'm asking because I bought a division of this same spectacular clone when I was there. It came labelled as "ornata Black Veins, Bulloch Co. GA" but sans any clonal designation, whereas all the clones do seem to have specific names. I know it can be hard to positively ID unlabeled individuals tho.

May 1, 2014 23:12:29 GMT -5 calen said:
"Damon's Clone" is is then! Here you go greenthumb - pics from 4/29.
There was an even nicer division on the sales floor, but right before I brought it over to the register a lady grabbed it first! As she was paying for it I heard her ask "So what do I grow this in?" A beautiful specimen, doomed most likely.
